sections.h2: Where is Caroline County, Virginia, and what kind of county is it?
sections.html:
Caroline County sits in eastern Virginia with the Rappahannock River along its northern edge. It is about 30 miles north of Richmond and 32 miles south of Fredericksburg, which puts it between two job centers.

The county covers 537 square miles and had 30,887 residents in the 2020 census. That is roughly double its population fifty years earlier, so many of the homes here are fairly recent additions to an older farming landscape. Bowling Green is the county seat and the largest town, and Port Royal is the only other incorporated town.

The county was established in 1727 and named for Queen Caroline of Ansbach. Tobacco and mixed farming shaped its early history, and later the county became known for thoroughbred horse farms. Secretariat, the 1973 Triple Crown winner, was born at The Meadow here.

sections.h2: What does the local economy mean for a house in Caroline County?
sections.html:
Most of the county economy is a mix of agriculture, distribution, military training and event business, and plenty of residents drive out of the county to work. A buyer or investor looking at a Caroline County house is often thinking about the commute along Interstate 95 as much as the lot itself.

  • Fort A.P. Hill, a military training complex of about 77,000 acres, was established in 1941.
  • The State Fair of Virginia moved to Meadow Event Park in 2009.
  • McKesson built a 340,000 square foot distribution center in the county.
  • M.C. Dean and Remuda Programs are other businesses named in the county's profile.

Caroline County Public Schools reported 490 employees in the 2020 to 2021 school year, including 209 teachers, so the school system is also a steady local employer.

sections.h2: Which highways and rail lines serve Caroline County?
sections.html:
Interstate 95 crosses the county, with exits 104 and 110, and U.S. Routes 1, 17 and 301 also run through it. State Routes 2, 30 and 207 fill in the local network.

Amtrak and CSX freight trains use the Richmond, Fredericksburg and Potomac rail corridor, which passes through Milford. For a seller, access to I-95 is usually the first thing a buyer asks about, and houses near an exit tend to be easier to describe than houses at the end of a long rural road.

sections.h2: When are Caroline County real estate taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate tax in Caroline County is due on June 5 and December 5. The county's own Dates to Remember page says a 10 percent penalty and 10 percent interest are added on June 6 and December 6 for real estate, personal property and business personal property.

ItemWhat the county lists
First installmentJune 5
Second installmentDecember 5
Penalty and interest10 percent each, added the next day
Water billsDue 15 days from the billing date
Dog tagJanuary 31
Business licenseMarch 1

Virginia law sets the outer limits. Under Code of Virginia 58.1-3916, a locality may charge interest of up to 10 percent a year and a penalty of up to 10 percent of the past-due property tax. The same section lets a locality waive both when the failure was not the taxpayer's fault, or when a payment was mailed on time with proof of mailing and arrived within five days of the deadline.

sections.h2: Who do you call at the Caroline County Treasurer and Commissioner of the Revenue?
sections.html:
The Treasurer collects the tax and the Commissioner of the Revenue handles assessment questions. They are separate offices with separate contacts.

  • Treasurer: 212 N Main Street, Bowling Green, VA 22427. Mail goes to P.O. Box 431. Phone 804-633-5291, open Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Real estate questions at the Commissioner's office: 804-633-9834 or realestate@co.caroline.va.us.
  • General county mail: P.O. Box 447, Bowling Green, VA 22427.

The Treasurer accepts payment online, by phone through ACI, by mail, in person, or by monthly automatic withdrawal. There is a drop box in front of the County Administration Building for after-hours payments. The county says it guarantees only payments made through its own website and Official Payments, so a payment sent through a personal bank bill-pay service is at the taxpayer's risk.

sections.h2: How do you check or appeal a Caroline County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the county's online assessment search and the Commissioner's real estate office, then use the Board of Equalization if you disagree. The county publishes a Real Estate Assessment Information tool at caroline.civ.quest, and a Tax Map page that shows parcels.

The county describes the appeal path this way. Owners with concerns about a reassessment first go to hearings with the Board of Assessors. A Board of Equalization is then set up to review complaints. It is a six member citizen panel, nominated by the Board of Supervisors and approved by a Circuit Court judge in each general reassessment year, and its members must complete training from the Virginia Department of Taxation. After the Board finishes, the county says the only option left is a petition to the Circuit Court under Section 58.1-3984 of the Code of Virginia.

State law helps the owner prepare. Under 58.1-3379, the assessor's value is presumed correct, and the owner must show it is above fair market value, applied unevenly, or not made under accepted appraisal practice. For a residential property with fewer than four units, the assessing officer must hand over the assessment records within 15 days of a written request.

sections.h2: What local rules matter when selling a house in Caroline County?
sections.html:
The main ones are building permits, land use programs, utilities and the recordation cost at closing. Each has its own office, so confirm them early.

  • Building permits: the county requires a permit before any new building, renovation, addition or major improvement, plus plumbing and mechanical permits. A certificate of occupancy is issued after satisfactory completion, and the Building Inspections office can be reached at 804-633-4303. Unpermitted work is worth sorting out before listing.
  • Land use: the Commissioner of the Revenue runs the land preservation program and rechecks each enrolled property every year. The county page does not list acreage or rollback rules, so ask that office if your parcel is enrolled.
  • Utilities: the county names the Carmel Church Ladysmith, Milford, Port Royal and Townfield water systems. Public Utilities is at 804-633-4390.
  • Elderly and disabled relief: questions go to the real estate office at 804-633-9834.

At closing, Virginia's grantor tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value, under 58.1-802. The statute puts it on the seller, though buyer and seller may agree otherwise.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Caroline County usually face with unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Sellers with unpaid tax usually face stacked penalty and interest and a larger payoff at closing. Because the county adds 10 percent penalty and 10 percent interest the day after each due date, a missed December 5 bill grows right away.

Ask the Treasurer for the balance on the day you expect to close, and ask the closing agent to confirm it. If the house needs work that a retail buyer would not accept, a cash buyer who purchases as is can save the repair and showing time, and the unpaid balance can be paid from proceeds at closing.

Cash Home Buyers can look at a Caroline County house with back taxes. We do not know your payoff for you, but we can plan around the figure the Treasurer gives you.

faqs.q: When are Caroline County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 and December 5. The county adds a 10 percent penalty and 10 percent interest on June 6 and December 6 for real estate and personal property.

faqs.q: Where is the Caroline County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: At 212 N Main Street in Bowling Green, open weekdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The phone number is 804-633-5291, and the mailing address is P.O. Box 431, Bowling Green, VA 22427.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Caroline County real estate assessment?
faqs.a: Talk to the Commissioner of the Revenue's real estate office first, then go to the Board of Equalization if you still disagree. After that, the county says the only remaining step is a Circuit Court petition under Section 58.1-3984 of the Code of Virginia.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Caroline County house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases the balance is paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for a current payoff figure and have your closing agent confirm it.

faqs.q: Who pays the Virginia grantor tax when a Caroline County house sells?
faqs.a: The statute puts the 50 cents per $500 grantor tax on the seller, but buyer and seller may agree that the buyer pays some or all of it.
